A couple of questions... 1) Why did you choose the enclosed track design? 2) You mentioned that the flopper stays in the extended position after pulling it open? If I understand you correctly, that's exactly what it's supposed to do. Once opened, it should lock into place so that it can't pull back through the fish. Or did I misunderstand you?

Well, you definitely don't want a free flowing flopper. You will lose fish. You want it to lock into position at about a 45 degree angle and not come back down on its own. Certain floppers tend to lock a little bit narrower than 45 degrees, but it's never caused a problem for me. If it's locking in the down position, that's bad and you definitely have a defective flopper. Here's a video that explains the flopper (a.k.a. barb) pretty well: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WN46te8xBWk

Usually, but if you don't get a kill shot and the fish is thrashing around, the flopper can come un-extended and the spear can slide out. It usually doesn't, but I've had it happen before. I was on a remote location and my flopper got damaged and was sticking in the down position, so I had to bend the metal so it wouldn't lock at all. I lost two fish on that trip because of the flopper.
